message.content: {"issues":[{"severity":"high","component":"harness.c D command / fire dispatch","trigger":"An event with a Bytes field inside a D command, or any fire() invocation from advance","why":"The D branch calls fire(&candidate,event,fields,byte_fields,-1,&log) but ignores its return value; a failed guard/action does not set failure, so committed=candidate commits a partially-mutated candidate (non-atomic failure). Similarly advance() calls fire(...) and aborts on 0, but D-path fire failure after advance leaves candidate timers already advanced and then still falls through to snapshot_fits/commit if fire returned 0 without setting failure. Failures must be atomic including prior timer steps, and a returning-0 fire must abort the whole operation and roll back to committed."},{"severity":"high","component":"harness.c D vs T ordering","trigger":"D command where at is in the past relative to m->now (advance returns 0 nonmonotonic) and event also present","why":"When advance fails, the code skips fire but still reaches snapshot_fits and commit if failure set by advance; however on nonmonotonic_time the candidate may have been partially advanced before discovering an out-of-order timer? No—advance checks at<m->now first. But for D with at>=now, advance commits timers via fire, then event fire runs even if a prior timer fire returned 0 is impossible; still the fire return is unchecked (see above). Distinct issue: for T commands the code calls invariants only in the else branch; if invariants(&candidate) returns 0 it is ignored and the candidate is committed regardless. State invariant violations are silently accepted."},{"severity":"high","component":"harness.c I command Bytes parse","trigger":"I command overriding a Bytes variable with an invalid token","why":"In the Bytes branch, parse_bytes returns 0 setting failure, but when parse_bytes succeeds failure remains NULL and snapshot_fits is called; however when parse_bytes fails the else-chain `if(!failure&&snapshot_fits...)` is skipped so error path is used — that part is fine. The real defect: when variable_kinds[index]==3 and parse_bytes fails, failure is set, but the surrounding code then tests `if(!failure&&snapshot_fits(&candidate))` — ok. But when kind!=3 and parse_integer/valid fails, failure set — ok. No issue beyond: the I command allows an integer-typed variable override but does not re-run invariants after override, so an initial override can violate state invariants yet still be committed. Spec expects invariants gating begin; an override that breaks invariants will only be caught at B if invariants checks. Acceptable only if B invariants is authoritative; still an override should be constrained to be consistent."},{"severity":"medium","component":"runtime.c byte_slice","trigger":"offset is a large positive int64 value","why":"`(uint64_t)offset>a.len` promotes offset to uint64; correct for nonnegative. But the spec defines slice as mathematical integers with max(0,offset); for offset between len and UINT64_MAX the cast is fine. For offset == INT64_MAX, (uint64_t)offset>a.len true, start=len. Correct. However count handling: `(uint64_t)count>a.len-start` where a.len-start is size_t; on platforms where size_t is 32-bit this is fine given cap 4096; on 64-bit fine. OK."},{"severity":"medium","component":"runtime.c text()","trigger":"Writing exactly fits LOG_CAP without room for NUL","why":"Condition `n>=LOG_CAP-b->size` rejects when n equals remaining, requiring n+1 bytes including NUL. This is conservative and correct (never truncates silently) but means the maximum usable payload is LOG_CAP-1; combined with snapshot_fits preview allowance LOG_CAP-1024, a snapshot near the limit could pass snapshot_fits (preview.size<=LOG_CAP-1024) yet fail during real snapshot because reply() prepends status JSON. Boundary: log exactly filling buffer."},{"severity":"medium","component":"harness.c reply() and log output","trigger":"log buffer near capacity or log text writes fail during fire","why":"text() inside fire/actions may set failure=\"output_capacity\" while the log is already partially written. The commit path checks snapshot_fits but not whether log writes succeeded before `failure` was set by a later text() call; if a fire action writes to log and sets failure mid-action, the fire return value is ignored in D (see above), so committed may advance even though the log was truncated. Atomicity of the visible log stream is also violated: fputs(log.data) only on success is fine, but a partial log is emitted only on failure path? On failure path reply prints error snapshot but log.data from candidate is discarded since committed log is separate—OK. Still, log capacity failure must roll back the whole operation."},{"severity":"medium","component":"runtime.c seqadd/distance and valid(kind 2)","trigger":"a or b = INT64_MIN passed to seqadd","why":"`a+b%SEQ_MOD` computed as int64 can overflow: b%SEQ_MOD is in (-MOD,MOD); a+b%SEQ_MOD can exceed INT64 range when a near INT64_MAX or INT64_MIN, invoking signed overflow UB before the % reduction. distance `(b-a+SEQ_MOD)%SEQ_MOD` likewise can overflow since b-a may exceed int64 range (a,b both in [0,MOD) so b-a in (-MOD,MOD), safe for distance; but seqadd receives raw a,b which may be arbitrary int64 via event fields before valid(), and kind 2 validation accepts n in [0,MOD) only, yet seqadd is a primitive that could be called with arbitrary a from other computed values). At minimum seqadd with a=INT64_MAX risks UB."},{"severity":"medium","component":"runtime.c parse_integer harness","trigger":"strtoll on value that overflows returns LONG_LONG range value and errno ERANGE","why":"parse_integer checks errno and *end and compares n to INT64_MIN/MAX; on 64-bit long long==int64 so the range compare is vacuous but errno catches overflow. On a platform where long long is wider than int64 this would catch; acceptable. However input value like \" 5\" with leading space: strtok already strips spaces so tokens have no spaces; fine. A token \"+5\" or \"-0\" accepted; JSON round-trip may differ but within native domain."},{"severity":"low","component":"harness.c input_capacity truncation","trigger":"Line longer than INPUT_CAP without newline","why":"On truncation the code sets failure=\"input_capacity\" then drains the rest of the line, but continues processing the truncated `line` with tokenization; since failure is set, the command is treated as an error reply, but partial tokens could have been parsed into fields/bytes before the check?
